title: show --json paths edge cases
lead: Three follow-ups from the s395 review of `show --json` `paths`. A root file that does not exist yet (or was deleted) can be named as `./NAME` so it counts as a path. `ops.item_file_paths` lists the project root only when there is a Files section to read. The docs say that only a space inside a span disqualifies it.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** guessing root files from git (`ls-tree HEAD`) or from slash-less names without `./`; changing which spans with a slash count; `overlap_ignore`; the 1.16 CHANGELOG entry, which is history and stays as written.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
From the s395 review (s395 added `paths` to `show --json`, commit 4cb1e1e). Checked against main at 4b32624 on 2026-11-02:

1. **A root file that is deleted or not yet created drops out of `paths`.** `paths.extract` (src/slicer/paths.py) admits a slash-less token only when it has a file extension and its name is in `top_level`. For `show`, `top_level` is `{entry.name for entry in state.root.iterdir()}` (ops.item_file_paths, src/slicer/ops.py:2317-2326). Probe: `extract("`CHANGELOG.md` `NEWS.md` `docs/new.md` `Makefile`", top_level={"CHANGELOG.md", "docs"})` returned `['CHANGELOG.md', 'docs/new.md']`. `NEWS.md`, which the slice will create, is gone. A file the slice deletes drops out as soon as it is deleted in the worktree. `docs/new.md` survives because a slash plus an extension needs no root match. The same extraction feeds `plan-parallel`, `next --batch --disjoint` and `deps --overlap`, so they miss the overlap too. The root check exists on purpose: it keeps bare names like `ai.py` or `config.json` in prose from counting as paths. So the spec does not drop the check. It lets an author mark a root path explicitly with a leading `./`, which today is only stripped. Owner question, with this answer recommended: a span that starts with `./` is a path whatever its root match or extension (`./NEWS.md`, `./Makefile`). The alternative is to document the limitation and change nothing.
2. **`item_file_paths` could short-circuit before `iterdir`.** It calls `state.root.iterdir()` first and only then `item_paths`, which returns `[]` for an item with no slice, no Files section or `files_section` unset (ops.py:2304-2314). `show` calls it for every item (cli.py, both the no-slice and the slice branch), so `show` of a bare row lists the project root for nothing.
3. **Docs inner-space wording.** docs/agents.md's `show ID` row (line 595) says "a span with a space ... is not a path". `extract` strips the span first (`span.strip()`), so a span with only surrounding spaces is a path. Probe: `` ` src/a.py ` `` gave `['src/a.py']`, while `` `src/a b.py` `` gave nothing. The rule is a space inside the span.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/paths.py` `extract`: note whether the stripped span started with `./` before removing it; such a token is admitted once it passes `_TOKEN` and is not empty after `strip("/")`. Update the docstring.
- `src/slicer/queries.py` `item_file_paths` (not ops.py; it moved): look up the slice and `files_section` first and return `[]` without listing the root when there is no section or its body is blank (`promote` seeds an empty Files section); call `paths.extract(section.body, top_level=...)` with the root names only after that. `item_paths` and its callers are unchanged.
- `docs/agents.md` line 609, the `show ID` row: "a span with a space" becomes "a span with a space inside it ... (surrounding spaces are trimmed)"; add that a span written with a leading dot-slash is a path even when no such root entry exists. `docs/configuration.md` line 126 (`files_section`) states the same rule.
- `tests/test_paths.py` for the `extract` tests; `tests/test_next.py` (`DisjointTests`, beside `test_Show_FilesSection_ListsPathSpansInJson`) for the `show` tests.
- `CHANGELOG.md` `## [Unreleased]` `### Changed`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Extract_DotSlashRootName_IsAPathWithoutARootMatch`: `extract("`./NEWS.md` `./Makefile` `NEWS.md`", top_level=set())` returns `['NEWS.md', 'Makefile']`. The bare `NEWS.md` stays out, and the dedup keeps one `NEWS.md`. Fails today (returns `[]`).
- `test_Show_NewRootFile_ListedWhenWrittenDotSlash`: an item whose Files section names `./NEWS.md` (absent from the fixture root) has `"NEWS.md"` in `show --json` `paths`; a bare `NEWS.md` item has none. Fails today.
- `test_Show_NoFilesToRead_DoesNotListTheRoot`: with `Path.iterdir` patched to raise `AssertionError` (only for the project root), `show ID --json` on a bare row and on a slice whose Files section is empty (as `promote` seeds it) exits 0 with `paths` `[]`. Fails today.
- `test_Extract_SurroundingSpaces_AreTrimmed`: `` ` src/a.py ` `` gives `src/a.py`; `` `src/a b.py` `` gives nothing. Passes today; it pins the documented rule.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests; watch the three fail.
2. The `./` rule in `extract`; the short-circuit in `item_file_paths`.
3. Docs and CHANGELOG. Run `-k '*Overlap*'` and `-k '*Disjoint*'` to confirm that `deps --overlap` and `next --batch --disjoint` still pass with the shared rule.

Owner decisions (2026-11-09): Does a leading `./` mark a Files span as a path, or is the limitation only documented? -> dot-slash rule: a ./-prefixed backtick span is a path whatever its root match or extension; a bare NEWS.md still needs a root match; plan-parallel, next --batch --disjoint and deps --overlap share the rule [paths.dot-slash-root-marker].

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- [ ] `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests -k '*Extract*'`, `-k '*Show*Paths*'`, `-k '*Overlap*'` and `-k '*Disjoint*'` pass.
- [ ] `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer show s413 --json --lean` still reports this slice's own paths.
- [ ] `python3 tests/affected.py --run`, the full suite, `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.
